headline: Record profit driven by one-time gains, not core operations
summary_short: GameStop's net sales were $835.3M, up 14.0% y/y but down 24.4% q/q, while net income of $389.6M (+769.6% y/y, a company record) was driven mainly by a $268.4M unrealized gain on its eBay-related derivative position rather than core operations.
summary_long: Net sales of $835.3M rose 14.0% y/y but fell 24.4% q/q, as collectibles grew to 41.8% of sales mix from 28.9% a year ago, offsetting hardware and software declines. SG&A fell to $201.6M from $228.1M, and the prior-year's $35.5M asset impairment did not recur, lifting GAAP operating income to $143.3M from a $10.8M loss. Net income of $389.6M, the highest in company history, was driven mainly by a $268.4M unrealized gain on eBay-related derivatives and $83.7M of net interest income on its $8.4B cash pile, not operating improvement. The board authorized a new $2.0B buyback through 2029. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Record net income was driven by collectibles growth, lower SG&A, and large one-time gains on eBay-related derivatives and interest income, not by core retail operating leverage.
Net sales grew 14% year-over-year, driven by collectibles; hardware and software categories both declined as a share of sales mix.
SG&A fell to $201.6M from $228.1M, and a $35.5M prior-year asset impairment (Canada/France divestitures) did not recur, versus a $4.6M net impairment reversal this quarter.
Driven mainly by a $268.4M unrealized gain on eBay-related derivative options, $83.7M of net interest income, and a $1.1M digital-asset gain, not by operating results.

The shard's operating-income-plus-D&A EBITDA proxy ($143.2M) differs sharply from the release's own reconciliation ($427.2M unadjusted / $163.4M adjusted), which includes the one-time derivative and digital-asset gains excluded here.
